newsitem.title: UK: Redwood claims growing support in UK Tory race.
newsitem.headline: Redwood claims growing support in UK Tory race.

text.p: John Redwood, claiming Conservatives were flocking to his Euro-sceptic banner, said on Monday he was the only one of the five leadership candidates who could revive the party because he was untainted by the policy errors and broken promies that cost it the general election.

Redwood told his last news conference ahead of Tuesday's first leadership ballot that he was best able to restore the Conservatives' reputation because he was not in the cabinet for the 22 months leading up to the May 1 election.

"Surely it is the one who did not go down in the ship who is best placed to launch and sail the new vessel," Redwood, who resigned as Welsh secretary in June 1995 to fight former prime minister John Major for the party leadership, said.
His campaign manager, Iain Duncan-Smith, said that in addition to the 17 Conservative MPs who have publicy declared their support for Redwood, another 30 had privately offered their backing.
Redwood refused to entertain any thought of doing deals if there is no outright winner in Tuesday's ballot of the party's 164 MPs.
"Me and my team are going to go the distance," he said.
Redwood said the election was a chance for Conservative MPs, by voting for him, to end the party's infighting over Europe by saying never' to the European single currency.
"The civil war will otherwise continue," he said.
